scenes.topic_description:
Situation: You arrive at the agency office before the viewing in Madrid. You need to check in, confirm that the appointment is for the right flat, and understand how the visit will start. You are renting with a small child, but family details are not discussed here.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Receptionist.
Not in this scene: room details, rent and deposit, documents, who will live in the flat, next steps after the viewing.

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: You are viewing the apartment with the agent in Madrid. This is the key interaction because you must decide whether the flat works for your situation and whether your small child can live there comfortably. What you understand here affects whether you continue with the application.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Real estate agent.
Not in this scene: checking in at the office, handing over documents, filling forms, signing a contract, paying money.

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: After the viewing, you decide to move forward and speak with the agent about the application. You need to understand the required papers, how to send them, and when you may get an answer. This is still before any contract signing.
Learner: Tenant. Partner: Real estate agent.
Not in this scene: first check-in, room details, rent discussion, living conditions in the flat, signing the lease.
